authors: McGaughey KD, Gold JI.
title: Sensory adaptation and pupil-linked arousal support flexible evidence accumulation during perceptual decision making.
design: Macaque RDK, MT recordings and pupillometry
verified_finding: Temporal context changes sensory adaptation and behavior; MT and pupil measures provide partly separate explanatory contributions.
limitation: Observational links do not identify an accumulator algorithm; adapter/test design differs from brief pulses.
proposed_next_test: Test context-dependent encoding before interpreting behavioral weighting as memory leak.

authors: Urai AE.
title: Structure uncovered: understanding temporal variability in perceptual decision-making.
verified_finding: Reviews temporal structure in perceptual decision variability.
limitation: Not primary evidence for this dataset or a new mechanism.
proposed_next_test: Use for citation chaining; do not count as an independent experiment.

authors: Duffy JS, Bellgrove MA, Murphy PR, O'Connell RG.
title: Disentangling sources of variability in decision-making.
verified_finding: Reviews the problem of assigning decision variability to specific processes.
limitation: Review synthesis is not a direct test of the proposed models.
proposed_next_test: Maintain separate sensory, policy and response hypotheses.

authors: Diaz JA, Pisauro MA, Delis I, Philiastides MG.
title: Prior probability biases perceptual choices by modulating the accumulation rate, rather than the baseline, of decision evidence.
design: Human choice/RT modeling constrained by EEG
verified_finding: Neural constraints shift the inferred source of prior-probability bias toward accumulation rate.
limitation: Independent neural constraints are unavailable in the reviewed mouse trial table.
proposed_next_test: Do not assign all history effects to starting point by default.

authors: Ueno T, Kumano H, Uka T.
title: Attention facilitates initiation of perceptual decision making: a combined psychophysical and electroencephalography study.
design: Human spatial cueing, motion discrimination and EEG
verified_finding: Valid cues affect sensory sensitivity and decision-related timing; CPP begins earlier.
limitation: Controlled spatial attention differs from uncued mouse motion; some modeling pooled participants.
proposed_next_test: The postdecision-delay null does not test variable sensory encoding or accumulation onset.

authors: Hulsey D, Zumwalt K, Mazzucato L, McCormick DA, Jaramillo S.
title: Decision-making dynamics are predicted by arousal and uninstructed movements.
design: Mouse visual/auditory discrimination, choices, omissions, pupil and movement
verified_finding: Persistent performance states covary with arousal and movement; prestimulus measures predict state occupancy.
limitation: State labels and physiological associations do not prove attention is the causal variable.
proposed_next_test: Assess serial structure and validate inferred states with outcomes excluded from state fitting.

authors: Calder-Travis J, Bogacz R, Yeung N.
title: Expressions for Bayesian confidence of drift diffusion observers in fluctuating stimuli tasks.
verified_finding: Defines trial-to-trial drift-rate scaling multiplicatively for time-varying sensory evidence.
limitation: A confidence derivation does not demonstrate that positive gain explains mouse pulse/RT data.
proposed_next_test: Multiplicative sensitivity is an established computational alternative, not a novel attention discovery.

authors: Stine GM, Zylberberg A, Ditterich J, Shadlen MN.
title: Differentiating between integration and non-integration strategies in perceptual decision making.
verified_finding: Specified nonintegration strategies can mimic conventional accumulation signatures.
limitation: Conclusions depend on task and tested candidate families.
proposed_next_test: Retain fair response-process assumptions and recovery for new comparisons.

authors: Pisupati S, Chartarifsky-Lynn L, Khanal A, Churchland AK.
title: Lapses in perceptual decisions reflect exploration.
design: Rat multisensory decisions, reward manipulations and neural disruption
verified_finding: Reward-dependent lapse patterns support uncertainty-guided exploration over a generic inattention explanation.
limitation: Reward manipulations and modalities differ from this mouse motion task.
proposed_next_test: Do not identify high-coherence errors or a fitted guess fraction as attention lapses.

authors: Urai AE, de Gee JW, Tsetsos K, Donner TH.
title: Choice history biases subsequent evidence accumulation.
design: Human perceptual decisions across task protocols
verified_finding: Choice repetition relates strongly to history-dependent accumulation bias, rather than only starting point.
limitation: Task-specific conditional RT predictions need simulation with this rig and stimulus.
proposed_next_test: Compare drift-bias and starting-point history mechanisms using conditional bias versus RT.

authors: Odoemene O, Pisupati S, Nguyen H, Churchland AK.
title: Visual Evidence Accumulation Guides Decision-Making in Unrestrained Mice.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
verified_finding: Visual accumulation in freely moving mice predates the present dataset.
limitation: Discrete visual pulses and response demands differ.
proposed_next_test: Frame novelty around constraints on variability, not the existence of mouse accumulation.

authors: Levi AJ, Yates JL, Huk AC, Katz LN.
title: Strategic and Dynamic Temporal Weighting for Perceptual Decisions in Humans and Macaques.
verified_finding: Temporal evidence weights adapt to the time course of stimulus information.
limitation: Experimentally manipulated statistics differ from the present fixed pulse schedule.
proposed_next_test: Treat temporal weighting as potentially strategic rather than a direct memory filter.

authors: Okazawa G, Sha L, Purcell BA, Kiani R.
title: Psychophysical reverse correlation reflects both sensory and decision-making processes.
verified_finding: Bounds, integration mechanisms and variable delays distort recovered sensory weights.
limitation: A kernel alone cannot distinguish those sources.
proposed_next_test: Forward-simulate the exact response-conditioned pulse estimator for every candidate.

authors: Murphy PR, Boonstra E, Nieuwenhuis S.
title: Global gain modulation generates time-dependent urgency during perceptual choice in humans.
design: Human deadline task, EEG, pupillometry and modeling
verified_finding: Speed pressure induces urgency-related motor preparation; pupil-linked gain is a candidate implementation.
limitation: Global neural gain is not equivalent to multiplying only the signed sensory input.
proposed_next_test: Keep sensory gain, evidence-independent urgency and bound changes distinct.

authors: Loughnane GM, Newman DP, Bellgrove MA, Lalor EC, Kelly SP, Kelly SP, O'Connell RG.
title: Target Selection Signals Influence Perceptual Decisions by Modulating the Onset and Rate of Evidence Accumulation.
design: Human uncertain target time/location with EEG
verified_finding: Target-selection signals modulate evidence accumulation onset and rate.
limitation: Human target selection is not directly measured in the mouse task.
proposed_next_test: Consider onset gating only if its pulse-time and RT signatures are supported.

authors: Murphy PR, Vandekerckhove J, Nieuwenhuis S.
title: Pupil-linked arousal determines variability in perceptual decision making.
design: Human motion discrimination, pupil and hierarchical DDM
verified_finding: Baseline pupil state relates to variability in evidence accumulation rate.
limitation: Correlational modeling does not uniquely separate between- and within-trial noise mechanisms.
proposed_next_test: Attention/arousal literature does not uniformly favor replacing additive drift variability.

authors: Brunton BW, Botvinick MM, Brody CD.
title: Rats and humans can optimally accumulate evidence for decision-making.
verified_finding: Controlled evidence permits quantitative modeling of accumulation and noise components.
limitation: Independent discrete samples offer identification advantages over correlated motion energy.
proposed_next_test: Separate sensory sample uncertainty from accumulation noise and latent sensitivity.

authors: Wong KF, Huk AC, Shadlen MN, Wang XJ.
title: Neural circuit dynamics underlying accumulation of time-varying evidence during perceptual decision making.
design: Recurrent circuit model of macaque motion pulses
verified_finding: Recurrent dynamics reproduce persistent pulse effects and timing dependence.
limitation: Computational agreement is not unique circuit identification.
proposed_next_test: Attractors remain an alternative, but a larger circuit model needs an additional discriminating signature.

authors: Wyart V, Myers NE, Summerfield C.
title: Neural mechanisms of human perceptual choice under focused and divided attention.
verified_finding: Divided attention can impair downstream integration while leaving encoded decision information available.
limitation: Two simultaneous streams differ substantially from the mouse single-stream task.
proposed_next_test: Attention can affect integration itself; do not reduce the entire literature to sensory gain.

authors: Stine GM, Trautmann EM, Jeurissen D, Shadlen MN.
title: A neural mechanism for terminating decisions.
verified_finding: Independent neural and causal measurements distinguish accumulation from decision termination.
limitation: Behavior-only data cannot support an equivalent circuit-level claim.
proposed_next_test: Use as a benchmark for specificity and calibrate the publication claim.

authors: Hyafil A, de la Rocha J, Pericas C, Katz LN, Huk AC, Pillow JW.
title: Temporal integration is a robust feature of perceptual decisions.
verified_finding: Designed evidence manipulations constrain integration versus nonintegration accounts.
limitation: Identification depends on input correlations and task structure.
proposed_next_test: Existing-data mechanism claims require recoverability within the actual design.

authors: Nunez MD, Vandekerckhove J, Srinivasan R.
title: How attention influences perceptual decision making: Single-trial EEG correlates of drift-diffusion model parameters.
design: Human noise/signal task, EEG-informed hierarchical DDM
verified_finding: Attention-related EEG measures predict drift and preprocessing time and modestly improve held-out prediction.
limitation: Error-RT prediction remains poor; neural features provide constraints absent here.
proposed_next_test: Test full choice/RT adequacy, not just a better correct-RT or choice fit.

authors: Ashwood ZC, Roy NA, Stone IR, International Brain Laboratory, Urai AE, Churchland AK, Pouget A, Pillow JW.
title: Mice alternate between discrete strategies during perceptual decision-making.
assessment: selected full text: author manuscript PDF
design: Mouse/human choice GLM-HMM with held-out comparisons
verified_finding: Persistent biased and stimulus-guided strategies explain serial choice structure; RT and omissions provide external checks.
limitation: State-conditioned RT checks are not a fitted joint choice/RT generative mechanism.
proposed_next_test: Compare static history, continuous change and a small HMM; validate pulse/RT consequences separately.

authors: Roy NA, Bak JH, International Brain Laboratory, Akrami A, Brody CD, Pillow JW.
title: Extracting the dynamics of behavior in sensory decision-making experiments.
assessment: selected full text: author PDF and PMC web
verified_finding: Continuous changes in sensitivity, bias and history weights can be inferred across trials and sessions.
limitation: Smoothed trajectories use future data and are not prestimulus causal states.
proposed_next_test: Compare continuous dynamics; use filtering or properly masked prediction for pulse tests.

authors: Goris RL, Movshon JA, Simoncelli EP.
title: Partitioning neuronal variability.
design: Macaque visual neuronal responses and modulated-Poisson modeling
verified_finding: Multiplicative excitability fluctuations explain neuronal variability and can have slow temporal correlations.
limitation: Includes anesthesia effects and is not a behavioral demonstration of attention.
proposed_next_test: Assess gain persistence rather than assuming an iid scalar gain is an attention model.

authors: Cheadle S, Wyart V, Tsetsos K, Myers N, de Gardelle V, Herce Castañón S, Summerfield C.
title: Adaptive gain control during human perceptual choice.
design: Human sequential evidence task with pupil/fMRI
verified_finding: Context-dependent gain favors evidence consistent with recent samples and predicts serial weighting.
limitation: This is not arbitrary amplification of surprising or strong pulses.
proposed_next_test: Require a signed context/congruency prediction before adding adaptive gain.

authors: Kelly SP, Kelly SP, O'Connell RG.
title: Internal and external influences on the rate of sensory evidence accumulation in the human brain.
verified_finding: Decision-signal buildup varies with coherence and endogenous attentional indices.
limitation: Neural covariation does not specify a unique gain distribution.
proposed_next_test: Sensory sensitivity is plausible, but computational parameters alone do not identify attention.

authors: Wyart V, de Gardelle V, Scholl J, Summerfield C.
title: Rhythmic fluctuations in evidence accumulation during decision making in the human brain.
verified_finding: Evidence weighting fluctuates with slow oscillatory phase rather than remaining constant within trials.
limitation: The present pulse schedule lacks a direct phase measure or broad phase-sampling design.
proposed_next_test: Do not fit an oscillatory attention account from a few response-conditioned pulse bins.

authors: Cohen MR, Maunsell JH.
title: Attention improves performance primarily by reducing interneuronal correlations.
verified_finding: Attention-related performance changes include altered interneuronal correlations.
limitation: Neural population noise is not identifiable from a scalar behavioral gain parameter.
proposed_next_test: Distinguish sensory noise, gain and decision noise.

authors: Smith PL, Ratcliff R.
title: An integrated theory of attention and decision making in visual signal detection.
verified_finding: Attention changes formation or onset of durable stimulus representations driving decisions.
limitation: A theoretical account is not direct validation in these mice.
proposed_next_test: Pure postdecision delay and evidence-encoding delay are different model tests.

authors: Reynolds JH, Heeger DJ.
title: The normalization model of attention.
design: Theoretical review introducing an attention normalization model
verified_finding: Normalization can produce distinct gain effects depending on stimulus and attention-field configuration.
limitation: Not new empirical evidence and not equivalent to the already fitted scalar normalization family.
proposed_next_test: Use for mechanisms and predictions, not as proof that another normalization fit will solve the mismatch.

authors: Chakravarty, Sucheta and Delgado-Sallent, Cristina and Kane, Gary A and Xia, Hongjie and Do, Quan H and Senne, Ryan A and Scott, Benjamin B
title: A cross-species framework for investigating perceptual evidence accumulation
verified_finding: Reports mouse behavior better described using multiple strategies in a cross-species evidence task.
limitation: Reviewed preprint; task and validation differ from these RDK pulses.
proposed_next_test: Constrain novelty to the joint RT/pulse variability problem.
